clue.text: Money consuming' festivity ?

parts.note: read as a feast that eats up beans, with 'bean' as slang for a coin, as in 'not a bean'

explanation.surface: A lavish party that eats through the cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bean' is old slang for money, so a festivity that consumes it is a feast of beans; the word is also British slang for a jolly works outing or celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: A beanfeast is a British term for a celebration or jolly outing, originally an employer's annual dinner for workers.

clue.text: Dance about and become a highwayman

indicators.note: the dance goes round, about, the word and

parts.note: the bolero is a Spanish dance

explanation.surface: Someone dances around and takes up robbery on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandolero is a Spanish bandit or highway robber.

clue.text: It could be a horse to put your shirt on!

definitions.text: It could be a horse to put your shirt on!

parts.words: It could be a horse to put your shirt on!
parts.note: a clothes horse on which to hang a shirt, not a racehorse to bet your shirt on

explanation.surface: A tip for a horse worth betting everything on.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'put your shirt on' a horse is to bet everything on it; here the horse is a clothes horse, a frame for drying laundry.
explanation.definitionFit: An airer is a clothes horse, a frame for drying washing.

clue.text: After justifiable arrest youth leader produces clean document (4; 4).

parts.note: fair means just or justifiable
to cop is to catch or arrest

indicators.note: the leader of the word youth is its first letter

explanation.surface: A youth leader produces a document after a legitimate arrest.
explanation.definitionFit: A fair copy is a clean final version of a document with corrections made.

clue.text: One month on an emperor's age

indicators.note: in a down clue the second piece follows on beneath the first

parts.note: August is a month of the year

explanation.surface: A month in the time of a Roman ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: The Augustan age was the reign of the emperor Augustus, a golden age of Latin literature.
explanation.definitionFit: Augustan describes the era of the emperor Augustus or a similar classical period.

clue.text: Unmanageable fellow to put up with rats.!

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting up lifts the letters to read from bottom to top

parts.note: the plural gives two rodents, rat and rat

explanation.surface: A difficult man asked to tolerate rodents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up with' looks like 'tolerate', but 'to put up' is the reversal signal for two RATS.
explanation.definitionFit: A tartar is a fierce, intractable person, hard to deal with.

clue.text: The nut from North Cape

indicators.note: the letters are made from the following words, rearranged into a new word

explanation.surface: A nut that comes from the far north of a country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is the anagram signal: the letters of N and CAPE are reworked.
explanation.definitionFit: The pecan is the edible nut of a North American hickory tree.

clue.text: Old writer's powder mixed in one cup

indicators.note: the letters of one cup are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Writing powder stirred into a single cup.
explanation.walkthrough: Pounce was a fine powder sprinkled on paper to stop ink spreading or dry it, used before blotting paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Pounce was the fine powder writers once sprinkled to prepare paper or dry ink.

clue.text: Feign illness, say, to get a drink?

indicators.note: the words are spoken out and the sound matched

parts.note: to fake suffering is to sham pain

explanation.surface: Faking sickness to be given a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Champagne is a sparkling wine from the French region of that name.

clue.text: They must, with old Nick at the wheel

definitions.text: They must, with old Nick at the wheel

parts.words: They must, with old Nick at the wheel
parts.note: from the proverb that one must when the devil drives; Old Nick is the devil

explanation.surface: People obliged to act because the devil is driving.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb is 'needs must when the devil drives'; 'Old Nick' is a name for the devil, here driving.
explanation.definitionFit: In the proverb, 'needs must' means necessity compels, when the devil is driving.

clue.text: Profession the railwaymen tunefully celebrate

parts.note: the NUR was Britain's National Union of Railwaymen
to celebrate in song is to sing

explanation.surface: Railway workers break into song in praise of a calling.
explanation.walkthrough: The NUR, the National Union of Railwaymen, was a British trade union, long familiar in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Caring for the sick is a vocation, a profession practised in hospitals.

clue.text: Boy in profligate musical run

indicators.note: the word for a boy sits inside the word for a profligate

parts.note: a roue is a dissolute, profligate man
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A young man caught up in a wild musical career.
explanation.definitionFit: In singing, a roulade is a rapid run of notes sung on one syllable.

clue.text: He blew hot and cold with Hamlet

definitions.text: He blew hot and cold with Hamlet

parts.words: He blew hot and cold with Hamlet
parts.note: the courtier in Shakespeare's play who agrees with the prince that the weather is cold, then that it is hot

explanation.surface: Someone who kept changing his mind alongside the Danish prince.
explanation.walkthrough: In Act 5 of Hamlet the foppish courtier Osric agrees first that it is cold, then that it is very sultry, as Hamlet teases him; 'blew hot and cold' is literal there.
explanation.definitionFit: Osric is the sycophantic courtier who agrees with every remark Hamlet makes about the weather.

clue.text: Not always the " big pictures ", but the main ones

definitions.text: Not always the " big pictures ", but the main ones

parts.words: Not always the " big pictures ", but the main ones
parts.note: 'the main' is the sea, so these are pictures of the main, not necessarily large canvases

explanation.surface: Artworks that are important without needing to be enormous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the main' is a poetic name for the open sea, so 'the main ones' are paintings of the sea, which are often large, though not always.
explanation.definitionFit: A seascape is a painting or view of the sea, the 'main' of old poetry.

clue.text: Perhaps a pure one in our -market

definitions.note: the setter means Britain's place in the Common Market, the European Economic Community

indicators.note: signals that the letters given may be rearranged into another word

explanation.surface: A virtuous person possibly found in our shopping arcade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' is the anagram signal on A PURE ONE. 'Our market' is the Common Market, as the European Economic Community was called when Britain joined.
explanation.definitionFit: Something belonging to the Common Market, the European Economic Community, is European.

clue.text: One out of place, if also running

definitions.text: One out of place, if also running

parts.words: One out of place, if also running
parts.note: an unplaced runner in a race is an also-ran

explanation.surface: Someone misplaced, who is also on the run.
explanation.walkthrough: In racing a horse 'out of place' finished outside the first three; an 'also ran' was running but unplaced.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner bred for the turf that finishes unplaced is an also-ran.

clue.text: He came delicately, 'but looked so silly going back

indicators.note: the word for silly is read from right to left

parts.note: gaga means senile or foolish

explanation.surface: A man who tiptoed in, but looked foolish on the way back.
explanation.walkthrough: In 1 Samuel 15, Agag king of the Amalekites 'came unto him delicately' before Samuel slew him.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bible's King Agag is described as coming to Samuel delicately, that is, cautiously.

clue.text: Jet cover provided for Fanny?

parts.note: a hood placed over a gas jet to give light, as in the film Fanny by Gaslight

explanation.surface: An aircraft hood made for a woman called Fanny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jet' is a gas jet, not an aircraft; 'Fanny by Gaslight' is a 1940 novel and 1944 British film.
explanation.definitionFit: A gas mantle is the incandescent mesh hood fitted over a gas jet to give light.

clue.text: A navy number in California revels

indicators.note: the navy number sits inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: RN, the Royal Navy
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Sailors celebrating in California.
explanation.definitionFit: A carnival is a festival of public merrymaking and revelry.

clue.text: Coal Burns ?'Sound idea, but this is cabbage

indicators.note: the clue words spoken out give the right noise

parts.note: coal plus Rabbie, the Scots name for the poet Robert Burns

explanation.surface: Is burning coal a good idea? No, this is rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Burns, Scotland's national poet, is 'Rabbie' Burns; 'coal Rabbie' sounds like the vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: Kohlrabi is a variety of cabbage grown for its swollen edible stem.

clue.text: Some touch of pain evokes this cry

indicators.note: only part of the word touch is wanted, its run of letters inside

explanation.surface: A slight painful contact makes someone yelp.
explanation.definitionFit: This exclamation is the usual cry of sudden pain.

clue.text: Gilbertian aristocratic Rogues' Gallery

parts.note: the line of wicked titled ancestors whose portraits come to life in Gilbert and Sullivan's Ruddigore

explanation.surface: A row of portraits of noble villains from a comic opera.
explanation.walkthrough: In Ruddigore, by W. S. Gilbert and Arthur Sullivan, the cursed Bad Baronets of Ruddigore step down from their picture gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: The ghostly ancestors in Ruddigore's picture gallery are the wicked titled heirs, holders of an hereditary rank below a peer.

clue.text: As stay-at-homes are, at — heart

definitions.meaning: split as ...: people who stay home are ... of the time

explanation.definitionFit: Split in two it says stay-at-homes are mostly indoors; whole, it means deepest within.

clue.text: Is in soft colour when forced open

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for soft

indicators.note: the word is goes inside the soft colour

parts.note: red is a colour

explanation.surface: Something is soft in colour when broken open.
explanation.definitionFit: Prised means levered or forced open.

clue.text: Knight who turned Elsa's brother out of the Swan

definitions.text: Knight who turned Elsa's brother out of the Swan

parts.words: Knight who turned Elsa's brother out of the Swan
parts.note: in Wagner's opera the swan-knight's swan is restored to human form as Elsa's lost brother Gottfried

explanation.surface: A hero who threw a lady's sibling out of a pub called the Swan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Swan' reads like a pub, but in Wagner's opera the swan that draws the knight's boat is Elsa's brother Gottfried, enchanted, and the knight turns it back into him.
explanation.definitionFit: Lohengrin is the title knight of Wagner's opera, who arrives in a boat drawn by a swan to defend Elsa.

clue.text: Endearing features ?

parts.note: parts of the ear, 'en-dearing' read as 'in the ear'

explanation.surface: Charming facial traits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endearing' hides 'ear'; the features found on an ear are the soft lower parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Lobes are the soft lower parts of the ears, features of the ear.

clue.text: Sign women's movement artist on

indicators.note: in an across clue the artist's letters are placed on after the movement's

parts.note: women's lib, the women's liberation movement
RA, Royal Academician, a British artist

explanation.surface: Feminists' symbol painted by a well-known artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Libra, the scales, is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: Tea bein made, he seems to growl

definitions.text: Tea bein made, he seems to growl

parts.words: Tea bein made, he seems to growl
parts.note: brewing tea, dropped g, is 'brewin'', which sounds like the name for a bear

explanation.surface: While tea is brewed, someone grumbles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tea bein' made' is 'brewin'', which sounds like Bruin, the traditional name for the bear, which growls.
explanation.definitionFit: Bruin is a traditional name for a bear, from the bear in the Reynard tales.

clue.text: Garment to produce intense heat round us'?

parts.note: to burn is to give off great heat
a round shape is the letter O

explanation.surface: Clothing that sets us sweltering.
explanation.definitionFit: A burnous is a long hooded cloak worn by Arabs and Berbers.

clue.text: It. bridges, the gap for those on the'high road

definitions.text: It. bridges, the gap for those on the'high road

parts.words: It. bridges, the gap for those on the'high road
parts.note: a raised road carried over a valley on arches

explanation.surface: Something that links travellers across a hollow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High road' is both a main road and, literally, a road carried high above the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A viaduct is a long bridge on arches carrying a road or railway across a valley.

clue.text: Steel, uncommonly cold in the fall.

indicators.note: the letters of steel are arranged in an unusual way

explanation.surface: Metal that is unusually cold when it drops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fall' is the falling of precipitation, not autumn.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleet is cold precipitation, part-frozen rain falling from the sky.

clue.text: Ophelia's primrose path

parts.note: Ophelia warns Laertes against treading 'the primrose path of' idle flirtation, in Hamlet

explanation.surface: The flowery way taken by Hamlet's sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: In Hamlet Act 1, Ophelia warns her brother not to preach virtue while himself treading 'the primrose path of dalliance'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ophelia's phrase links the primrose path with flirtatious, idle pleasure-seeking.
